release: DNS & CUTOVER IS TOOL 5. Every check this engine performs began AFTER the domain had already resolved, which left a migration's most expensive failures structurally invisible: a nameserver swap that drops MX and SPF takes a business's email down while every page still scores 100. lib/dns adds three actions matching the three moments of a migration - CAPTURE the zone plus what the current origin serves BEFORE the cutover, which is the only way a later run can tell a DELETED record from one that never existed; VERIFY diffs against that baseline and proves the new origin actually serves with a certificate that covers the name; RECOVER reads the zone the replaced nameservers usually still hold and rebuilds the baseline after the fact, including the subdomains nobody remembers exist. SCORE-NEUTRAL BY CONSTRUCTION - suite weight 0 and every rule severity manual, because a Site Audit routinely runs against a domain the operator does not control and a scored DNS suite would deduct for someone else's nameservers on every run, and would make the score depend on the auditing machine's network path. The registry is UNTOUCHED at 161 rules and 1.15.0; the 29 DNS rules live in their own module and move no score. NEVER THE SYSTEM RESOLVER - four named public resolvers, reported individually, because disagreement between them IS the propagation signal; ENODATA is not ENOTFOUND, and a timed-out resolver is excluded from consensus rather than counted as agreement, so a network hiccup can never render as 'MX unchanged'. FOUR DEFECTS WERE FOUND BY A LIVE RUN AFTER 361 OFFLINE ASSERTIONS WERE ALREADY GREEN: SOA normalised from the wrong shape, www probed with the wrong object so every www reported a FABRICATED outage, a null MX read as real mail routing, and a machine with no IPv6 route reporting the SITE as degraded - a limit of the auditing host presented as a defect of the audited site. FOUR MORE were found only by RENDERING the UI after every DOM assertion passed: stale 'five tools' copy, a bare '0' for the null MX, an Agreement column that rendered empty on a clean run so the reader could not tell 'all agreed' from 'never checked', and DNS-008 firing on every routine re-check because expectCutover existed in the library and had never been exposed. 6.4.1 EXISTS BECAUSE OF THIS FILE: 6.4.0 was published with engine/package.json at 6.4.0 and this metadata still at 6.3.0 - release-gate.js caught it, which is precisely the drift it was written for, and the payload was corrected forward rather than republished under the same number. Previous release: Autonomous pass over the highest-value unfinished work. Four units, none of which crossed the Architecture Freeze. GZIPPED SITEMAPS ARE PARSED. They were recorded present-and-unread because getText decodes UTF-8, which destroys gzip bytes; zlib is a builtin so this cost no dependency. Gzip is detected by MAGIC BYTES, covering a raw .gz file, a Content-Encoding gzip response, and a .gz extension on plain XML. Decompression is capped at 64 MB because a few hundred bytes of gzip can encode gigabytes and an unbounded gunzip in a tool that fetches attacker-controlled URLs is a denial-of-service the AUDITED SITE can aim at the operator. Size accounting uses the UNCOMPRESSED length, or a 2 MB gzip carrying 80 MB of XML would pass a limit it plainly breaks. THE TWO NUMBERS EXPLAIN THEMSELVES. A run read 'score 50, quality 84, PASSED WITH WARNINGS' with no statement of what any of them measures and two apparently contradicting. Both are now labelled and carry the reason they differ: one is the share of GRADED checks that passed, weighting every check equally; the other is registry-weighted over rules that provably ran, so one critical failure costs more than ten minor ones. Presentation only - the scoring model is frozen and nothing recomputes it. TEST-SUITE ENVIRONMENT SWEEP, after the PID-modulo port. ui-script.test.js derived its port from hrtime and then CONNECTED to it, the same silent talk-to-a-stranger class; it now asks the OS for a free port AND aborts if the spawned child died, so asserting against another process is impossible rather than unlikely. Two fixture suites moved off fixed ports. AND THE REAL FIND: three suites pin assertions to stored live runs that HAVE BEEN DELETED, so roughly fourteen assertions in readiness plus the anti-fixture cross-check in score-evaluation have been silently dead while the run reported 66/66. Not fixable by inventing baselines - re-pinning to a current run means deriving expectations from today's behaviour, the exact trap those suites exist to prevent. The skip is now LOUD and NAMES the missing artifacts. CERTIFICATION.md MATCHES THE PRODUCT AGAIN. The record that answers 'can this ship' claimed engine 2.4.0, registry 1.13.0, 142 rules, package 4.5.0 and 58 suites while the product was 4.1.0, 1.15.0, 161, 6.2.0 and 66 - drifted through two majors with nothing to catch it. Reconciled, and now GUARDED by verifyCertification() in the version-authority suite, with a negative control that proves the verifier reports dirty on a deliberately stale copy.
